scope: Theorem 6.4 (Uniform excess propagation) of the manuscript “Riesz transforms and uniform rectifiability in higher codimension” (preprints/Riesz-transforms-and-uniform-rectifiability-in-higher-codimension-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 081 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8445a9b1c8e5a4c3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 46. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix 1 ≤ n < d, c, G > 0, D0 ≥ 0, 0 < γ < 1/2, and ε > 0. For every integer J0 ≥ 0, there is an integer J ≥ J0, depending only on these fixed data, with the following property. Set δ = 2−J , K = 2J + 3, A = 8 2K . (6.22) Let µ satisfy (6.1)–(6.3), let a ∈ supp µ, and let r > 0. Assume 2K r ≤ diam(supp µ), (6.23) eµ(a, 2ℓ r) ≤ δ2γℓ (0 ≤ ℓ ≤ K), (6.24) and assume |Rµ(φ)| ≤ δ3 rn (6.25) for every compactly supported scalar function φ satisfying Lip(φ) ≤ r−1 , supp φ ⊂ B(a, Ar), Z φ dµ = 0. Then eµ(a, r/2) ≤ δ, bµ(a, r/2) < ε. (6.26) Equivalently, the oscillation hypothesis can be stated with Lip(φ) ≤ 1 and threshold δ3rn+1. The constants J, δ, K, A are chosen before the measure, center, and radius. The test radius Ar need not be admissible.
